items.title: Pentagon to take 35% stake in Venezuela oil venture, WSJ reports
items.summary: Investing.com -- The Pentagon plans to take a 35% passive stake in a private company holding Venezuelan oil rights, marking an unusual expansion of the U.S. government’s role from facilitating energy investment to directly owning an interest in an oil venture, the Wall Street Journal reported exclusively.

items.title: Trump Venezuela oil deal draws criticism from government allies, opposition
items.summary: Investing.com -- U.S. President Donald Trump’s oil agreement with Venezuela is drawing criticism from both hard-line supporters of the country’s government and opposition forces, putting acting President Delcy Rodríguez under growing political pressure, Bloomberg reported.

items.title: The Number ExxonMobil No Longer Puts In Front Of Its Results
items.summary: Management's own scorecard still leads with dollars, but the return measure that used to sit beside it was absent again, and that changes what a holder is actually betting on.

items.title: Devon Energy vs. ConocoPhillips: Which Oil Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Devon Energy looks cheaper than ConocoPhillips, while both offer shale-led growth, rising cash flow prospects and sizable shareholder-return plans.

items.title: Chevron Could Be Big Winner If Venezuela Pulls Out of OPEC
items.summary: Venezuela is edging away from OPEC, U.S. companies are circling its vast untapped oil fields, and one American energy giant already has a foot in the door before the bidding even begins.

items.title: ExxonMobil Stock's Biggest Risk Is The Shortage Ending
items.summary: ExxonMobil's refining and chemical margins rest on capacity that is offline elsewhere, which makes a return to normal supply the risk worth weighing.

items.title: Equinor starts production at Troll phase three, stage two in North Sea
items.summary: The project is set to accelerate the recovery of around 55bscm of gas from the Troll West reservoir.
